before.title: Primary FSGS with APOL1 branch
before.diseaseDescription: Bounded circulating-factor/immune primary FSGS and separate APOL1-associated kidney injury branch; excludes other genetic, adaptive, viral and drug-associated FSGS. APOL1-associated disease is not classified as idiopathic primary FSGS. Selected mechanistic and intervention reports; not comprehensive literature or treatment coverage.
before.releaseNote: Initial bounded source-checked candidate. Agent inspected indexed primary abstracts; independent domain review pending. Conflicting anti-nephrin and negative suPAR findings retained. No complete therapy coverage.

after.title: Primary FSGS with APOL1 branch
after.diseaseDescription: Bounded circulating-factor/immune primary FSGS and separate APOL1-associated kidney injury branch; excludes other genetic, adaptive, viral and drug-associated FSGS. APOL1-associated disease is not classified as idiopathic primary FSGS. Selected mechanistic and intervention reports; not comprehensive literature or treatment coverage.
after.releaseNote: Separate study-context views for primary FSGS serum activity, human anti-nephrin findings, experimental immune injury, APOL1 ion transport, transgenic injury, inaxaplin trial and DUPLEX. No universal causal circuit or comprehensive therapy catalogue. Source checks are agent abstract inspections; independent scientific review pending.

before.text: Induced G1 expression produced sodium import and potassium efflux in HEK293 experiments.
limitations: Overexpression system; G1 result does not by itself establish identical G2 effects or penetrance in humans.

after.text: Induced G1 expression produced sodium import and potassium efflux in HEK293 experiments.
limitations: Overexpression system; G1 result does not by itself establish identical G2 effects or penetrance in humans.

before.text: Patient-derived anti-CD40 antibodies were studied in human podocyte injury assays with rescue by pathway blockade.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: Patient-derived anti-CD40 antibodies were studied in human podocyte injury assays with rescue by pathway blockade.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

before.text: IFNγ-induced APOL1 G1 in transgenic mouse podocytes produced ion-flux and injury phenotypes reversible by VX-147.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: IFNγ-induced APOL1 G1 in transgenic mouse podocytes produced ion-flux and injury phenotypes reversible by VX-147.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

before.text: Circulating permeability activity was associated with FSGS recurrence after transplantation.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: Circulating permeability activity was associated with FSGS recurrence after transplantation.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

before.text: Interferon gamma induced an APOL1-dependent cation current in primary human podocytes.
limitations: Culture response; not proof that interferon is required in every APOL1-associated patient.

after.text: Interferon gamma induced an APOL1-dependent cation current in primary human podocytes.
limitations: Culture response; not proof that interferon is required in every APOL1-associated patient.

before.text: Inaxaplin inhibited APOL1 channel function in preclinical cell assays.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: Inaxaplin inhibited APOL1 channel function in preclinical cell assays.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

before.text: In a single-group phase 2a study, 13 adherent participants with two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS had a mean 47.6% proteinuria reduction at 13 weeks.
limitations: Uncontrolled small short-term trial; no randomized effect estimate, established kidney-survival benefit or approval inference.

after.text: In a single-group phase 2a study, 13 adherent participants with two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS had a mean 47.6% proteinuria reduction at 13 weeks.
limitations: Uncontrolled small short-term trial; no randomized effect estimate, established kidney-survival benefit or approval inference.

before.text: Increasing experimental podocyte depletion caused persistent proteinuria in transgenic rats.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

after.text: Increasing experimental podocyte depletion caused persistent proteinuria in transgenic rats.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

before.text: Toxin-induced podocyte depletion produced focal segmental sclerosis in transgenic rats.
limitations: Generic final-pathway animal model; does not establish the initiating mechanism in primary human FSGS.

after.text: Toxin-induced podocyte depletion produced focal segmental sclerosis in transgenic rats.
limitations: Generic final-pathway animal model; does not establish the initiating mechanism in primary human FSGS.

before.text: Nephrin-directed antibodies localized to the slit diaphragm in an active-immunization mouse model.
limitations: MCD-like mouse model; not a demonstration of human FSGS sclerosis or universal antibody causation.

after.text: Nephrin-directed antibodies localized to the slit diaphragm in an active-immunization mouse model.
limitations: MCD-like mouse model; not a demonstration of human FSGS sclerosis or universal antibody causation.

before.text: A Chinese cohort including 160 primary FSGS and 436 MCD patients reported anti-nephrin reactivity; its 43% overall prevalence is pooled across diagnoses.
limitations: Pooled result must not be reported as FSGS-specific prevalence; assay/cohort differences remain unresolved.

after.text: A Chinese cohort including 160 primary FSGS and 436 MCD patients reported anti-nephrin reactivity; its 43% overall prevalence is pooled across diagnoses.
limitations: Pooled result must not be reported as FSGS-specific prevalence; assay/cohort differences remain unresolved.

before.text: Anti-nephrin antibodies were detected in 7 of 74 adults (9%) with primary FSGS in the multicenter study.
limitations: Minority subgroup; activity correlations and experimental MCD-like findings cannot be assigned to all FSGS.

after.text: Anti-nephrin antibodies were detected in 7 of 74 adults (9%) with primary FSGS in the multicenter study.
limitations: Minority subgroup; activity correlations and experimental MCD-like findings cannot be assigned to all FSGS.

before.text: A separate podocytopathy cohort found very low anti-nephrin prevalence with human-cell antigen and no disease enrichment, challenging broad biomarker interpretation.
limitations: Mixed podocytopathies, not a primary-FSGS-only estimate; does not exclude a rare pathogenic subset.
Antigen-dependent cross-reactivity materially limits cross-study comparison.

after.text: A separate podocytopathy cohort found very low anti-nephrin prevalence with human-cell antigen and no disease enrichment, challenging broad biomarker interpretation.
limitations: Mixed podocytopathies, not a primary-FSGS-only estimate; does not exclude a rare pathogenic subset.
Antigen-dependent cross-reactivity materially limits cross-study comparison.

before.text: Serum from recurrent FSGS patients increased albumin permeability in an isolated-glomerulus assay.
limitations: Ex vivo assay does not identify the factor, prove clinical causation, or apply to all primary FSGS.

after.text: Serum from recurrent FSGS patients increased albumin permeability in an isolated-glomerulus assay.
limitations: Ex vivo assay does not identify the factor, prove clinical causation, or apply to all primary FSGS.

before.text: Despite greater proteinuria reduction, DUPLEX found no significant between-group eGFR-slope difference at 108 weeks.
limitations: Surrogate improvement must not be described as demonstrated overall trial kidney-function preservation.

after.text: Despite greater proteinuria reduction, DUPLEX found no significant between-group eGFR-slope difference at 108 weeks.
limitations: Surrogate improvement must not be described as demonstrated overall trial kidney-function preservation.

before.text: DUPLEX showed greater partial proteinuria remission with sparsentan than irbesartan at 36 weeks (42% versus 26%).
limitations: Mixed FSGS eligibility; not proof of immunologic mechanism or applicability of current indication to nephrotic primary FSGS.

after.text: DUPLEX showed greater partial proteinuria remission with sparsentan than irbesartan at 36 weeks (42% versus 26%).
limitations: Mixed FSGS eligibility; not proof of immunologic mechanism or applicability of current indication to nephrotic primary FSGS.

before.text: suPAR-associated podocyte injury in patient-serum culture assays was inhibited by anti-uPAR blockade.
limitations: Culture blockade does not establish suPAR as a universal circulating cause or an effective clinical target.

after.text: suPAR-associated podocyte injury in patient-serum culture assays was inhibited by anti-uPAR blockade.
limitations: Culture blockade does not establish suPAR as a universal circulating cause or an effective clinical target.

before.text: Serum suPAR was not significantly higher in the FSGS group in a prospective Brazilian biopsy cohort.
limitations: FSGS classification not restricted to primary disease; biomarker specificity test does not directly refute culture toxicity.
Indirect qualification of generalizing the suPAR injury hypothesis; this is a biomarker null finding, not a direct culture replication.

after.text: Serum suPAR was not significantly higher in the FSGS group in a prospective Brazilian biopsy cohort.
limitations: FSGS classification not restricted to primary disease; biomarker specificity test does not directly refute culture toxicity.
Indirect qualification of generalizing the suPAR injury hypothesis; this is a biomarker null finding, not a direct culture replication.
